title: Observer pattern

overview.why: It keeps your code uncoupled. The publisher does not need to know the exact details of every subscriber. It just sends the message. You can add 100 new subscribers without changing the publisher code.
where_used: User interface buttons (clicking a button notifies the app)
Sending emails when a database record changes

why_learning_this: You will understand how event-driven systems (like clicking buttons) work.
You will know how to separate the code that creates data from the code that displays it.

common_mistakes.title: Forgetting to unsubscribe
common_mistakes.explanation: If an object is no longer needed but is still in the publisher's list, Python will never delete it. This wastes memory and can cause weird bugs where deleted users still receive messages.

common_mistakes.title: Slow observers blocking everything
common_mistakes.explanation: The publisher updates observers one by one. If one observer takes 10 seconds to process the news, everyone else has to wait. Keep observer methods fast.

recall_questions.q: Explain the Observer pattern in your own words, as if to a classmate.
recall_questions.answer: The Observer pattern is when one central object keeps a list of other objects. When something new happens, it loops through the list and sends a message to everyone.

recall_questions.q: Why is this better than having the subscribers constantly ask "is there new data?"
recall_questions.answer: Because constantly asking wastes time and computer power. With this pattern, they just wait, and the data comes to them immediately when it is ready.

recall_questions.q: What happens if you delete a subscriber in your code but forget to remove it from the publisher's list?
recall_questions.answer: The publisher still holds a reference to it. The subscriber will not be fully deleted from memory (a memory leak) and will keep receiving updates.

understanding_checks.question: Why does this code crash?
understanding_checks.answer: Because it tries to call the `Display` object like a function `screen(temp)` instead of calling its method `screen.show(temp)`.
understanding_checks.why: The publisher must call a specific method on the observer. Objects cannot usually be called directly with parentheses unless they have special magic methods.

aha_moment.prediction: What does this print? Look closely at what we appended to the list.
aha_moment.common_guess: It crashes because `print_hello` is not an object.
aha_moment.why: In Python, functions ARE objects! You do not always need a class to be an observer. You can just append a simple function to the list, and the publisher can call it.
